what: is another rover's position report wrong? a small network against chi-square, CUSUM and logistic regression at the same false-alarm rates
params_note: Values come from section D ('Simulation parameters for the backend engineer') of research_notes/Lunar Rover Interaction Protocol/01_positioning_and_time.md (11 Nov 2026). Source keys in square brackets and the tags MOON / MARS / EARTH / SIM / REQ / CALC are that note's; 'A' is that note's mark for an assumption anchored on its sources but not measured. Parameters listed under not_in_note_01 are not in the note's table: they are the task's values or B-96 assumptions and have no opened external source.

params_source.uwb_range_noise_m: note 01 D: 'UWB two-way range error, line of sight' [PLANS18, NUCH24] EARTH
params_source.uwb_range_max_m: note 01 D: 'UWB maximum range', A (no lunar value is public; vendor claim of 290 m UNVERIFIED)
params_source.long_range_noise_m: note 01 D: 'Long-range two-way ranging over the base radio (S-band or cellular)', A
params_source.long_range_cap_m: note 01 D gives the limit as 'radio line of sight from existing notes'; here: the smooth-Moon mutual horizon sqrt(2 R h_a) + sqrt(2 R h_b), R = 1,737.4 km (research_notes/Lunar ATC/vehicles_comms_internals.md section 2.5, Computed), with the trace's antenna heights, and at most this cap = the engine's radio range d_max (lunarsim/atc/radio.py, provisional B-70). Terrain blocking is not modelled.
params_source.nlos_bias_m: note 01 D: 'Range bias when the direct path is blocked', A
params_source.dr_error_frac: note 01 D: 'Dead-reckoning drift, firm level ground, VO + star tracker' [MAIM07] EARTH; [DAF23, ATHA24] REQ
params_source.dr_error_frac_loose_no_vo: note 01 D: 'Dead-reckoning drift, loose soil or slope above 10 deg, no VO' [HELM06] EARTH
params_source.fix_sigma_m: note 01 D: 'Absolute fix accuracy, terrain matching, sunlit' [DAF23] REQ (5 m at 3-sigma); lower end [NASH24] MARS
params_source.fix_spacing_m: note 01 D: 'Distance between terrain-fix opportunities, sunlit highlands', A

ood_setting.note: out-of-distribution test set: the true errors change, the values A's filter assumes (above) do not
ood_setting.source: LEAD, task B-96; 0.05 is the low end of note 01 D's loose-soil range, 2 x 0.3 m and 2 x 3 m are inside its ranging sweeps

false_alarm_definition: a 60 s bin of fault-free stream with at least one step above threshold; rates are weighted to the natural share of blocks with and without driving

model.int8_note: one byte per weight, a 32-bit bias per output channel and one 32-bit scale per layer; an estimate, the int8 network was not built or tested

baselines.rule: W, k and CUSUM variant: best mean of the validation macro event recall at 1 per pair-day and at 1 per pair-hour

timing.note: one whole window recomputed per report (no reuse of the previous window's activations)

landscape.note: gap = |loss on the plane - loss recorded at the checkpoint| on the validation subset; 'projection' evaluates the plane exactly at the projected point, 'nearest node' at the closest grid node (what the page shows)

h15_resample_counts_b118.note: B-118 N8: the bootstrap resample counts behind H15's comparisons (h15_block at 1 false alarm per pair-day), reproduced from the saved event arrays (EVAL_CACHE) with the same random streams as the published evaluation, and checked against the stored intervals. Written to results/E56_integrity.json under a new top-level key; every other key is left as it is. A one-sided bootstrap p for 'network shorter' is (at_or_above_0 + 1) / (boot_n + 1).

onset_context_and_fa_interval_b118.note: B-118 N10 and N11, from the saved scores (.cache/nn/scores_final_*.npz) and the stored validation thresholds; nothing is retrained or recalibrated, and every existing key of results/E56_integrity.json is left as it is. N10: beside each recall (test and out-of-distribution sets, both rates, per fault type and overall), the share of events with an alarm already on at the step before onset (baselines.onset_context), and the recall on the events with no alarm in the 60 s before onset. N11: the false-alarm interval on all 1,000 resamples (the published one used the first 200), with the same resample indices. Every recomputed recall and 200-resample interval is checked against the stored value first.
